Topics · Meaning and purpose

Why does religion start with death, not life?

The Quran names death and life together and sets their purpose as a question of life: whose conduct is best.

Part 1 of 3

﴿ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلْمَوْتَ وَٱلْحَيَوٰةَ لِيَبْلُوَكُمْ أَيُّكُمْ أَحْسَنُ عَمَلًا ۚ وَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْغَفُورُ﴾

Translation of the meaning

[He] who created death and life to test you [as to] which of you is best in deed - and He is the Exalted in Might, the Forgiving -

Quran · Al-Mulk 67:2

Translation

I know also, my God, that you try the heart and have pleasure in uprightness. As for me, in the uprightness of my heart I have willingly offered all these things. Now I have seen with joy your people, who are present here, offer willingly to you.

Original · Hebrew

וְיָדַ֣עְתִּי אֱלֹהַ֔י כִּ֤י אַתָּה֙ בֹּחֵ֣ן לֵבָ֔ב וּמֵישָׁרִ֖ים תִּרְצֶ֑ה אֲנִ֗י בְּיֹ֤שֶׁר לְבָבִי֙ הִתְנַדַּ֣בְתִּי כָל־אֵ֔לֶּה וְעַתָּ֗ה עַמְּךָ֙ הַנִּמְצְאוּ־פֹ֔ה רָאִ֥יתִי בְשִׂמְחָ֖ה לְהִֽתְנַדֶּב־לָֽךְ׃

1 Chronicles · 29:17

World English Bible

Your teacher's instinct is sound: someone who has not yet learned to live has little to ask about death. This passage holds the same instinct. It names life and death together and gives their purpose as a question about life, which of you does best in deed. Here death enters the sentence to make life matter. What counts is the doing, here and now.

A question for you

What would you most want said about your life?

If you sayThat I was fair to people.
ThenFairness is the first thing named in the third passage.
If you sayThat I looked after my family.
ThenFamily is named in the third passage too.
If you sayThat I learned and kept growing.
ThenGrowing belongs to the same picture. The next passage looks at what grows in a person.

Part 2 of 3

﴿وَنَفْسٍ وَمَا سَوَّىٰهَا٧ فَأَلْهَمَهَا فُجُورَهَا وَتَقْوَىٰهَا٨ قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن زَكَّىٰهَا٩ وَقَدْ خَابَ مَن دَسَّىٰهَا١٠﴾

Translation of the meaning

And [by] the soul and He who proportioned it[1932] And inspired it [with discernment of] its wickedness and its righteousness, He has succeeded who purifies it, And he has failed who instills it [with corruption].

Translator's notes

[1932] i.e., balanced and refined it, creating in it sound tendencies and consciousness.

Quran · Ash-Shams 91:7-10

Translation

(for when Gentiles who don’t have the law do by nature the things of the law, these, not having the law, are a law to themselves, in that they show the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience testifying with them, and their thoughts among themselves accusing or else excusing them)

Original · Ancient Greek

ὅταν γὰρ ἔθνη τὰ μὴ νόμον ἔχοντα φύσει τὰ τοῦ νόμου ποιῶσιν, οὗτοι νόμον μὴ ἔχοντες ἑαυτοῖς εἰσιν νόμος· οἵτινες ἐνδείκνυνται τὸ ἔργον τοῦ νόμου γραπτὸν ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις αὐτῶν, συμμαρτυρούσης αὐτῶν τῆς συνειδήσεως καὶ μεταξὺ ἀλλήλων τῶν λογισμῶν κατηγορούντων ἢ καὶ ἀπολογουμένων,

Romans · 2:14-15

World English Bible

Many teachers hold that a person becomes good by tending the heart. This passage says something close about the soul: it was shaped well, it was given an inner sense of what spoils it and what protects it, and the one who thrives is the one who tends it. The work is daily and small, and it starts from a sense you already have.

A question for you

What do you tend most in yourself?

If you sayMy patience.
ThenPatience is built by small repeats, which is what the passage describes: daily work, not a speech.
If you sayMy honesty.
ThenHonesty starts with recognising a wrong when you see it, which is the sense the passage speaks of.
If you sayMy kindness to people.
ThenThat is among the first things the next passage asks for.

Part 3 of 3

﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأْمُرُ بِٱلْعَدْلِ وَٱلْإِحْسَـٰنِ وَإِيتَآئِ ذِى ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ وَيَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنكَرِ وَٱلْبَغْىِ ۚ يَعِظُكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Indeed, Allāh orders justice and good conduct and giving [help] to relatives and forbids immorality and bad conduct and oppression. He admonishes you that perhaps you will be reminded.

Quran · An-Nahl 16:90

Translation

Therefore turn to your God. Keep kindness and justice, and wait continually for your God.

Original · Hebrew

וְאַתָּ֖ה בֵּאלֹהֶ֣יךָ תָשׁ֑וּב חֶ֤סֶד וּמִשְׁפָּט֙ שְׁמֹ֔ר וְקַוֵּ֥ה אֶל־אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ תָּמִֽיד׃

Hosea · 12:6

World English Bible

Here is what the passage asks, plainly: justice, kindness, giving to relatives; and staying clear of what is shameful, what is hateful, and what oppresses. A teacher could read it aloud in any town. It is a way of living before it is anything else. If you wondered whether religion is only talk about death, this verse is about the street, the shop and the family table.

A question for you

Which of the three is hardest for you: justice, kindness, or care for family?

If you sayJustice, because it costs.
ThenThat may be why it comes first in the list: it is never done for free.
If you sayKindness, because no one is checking.
ThenKindness is doing more good than is owed, which is close to what the word means.
If you sayFamily, because it never ends.
ThenIt is a task for a lifetime, and the verse sets it right beside justice.

The same in the other books

Translation

For the wisdom of the Lord is great. He is mighty in power, and sees all things. His eyes are upon those who fear him. He knows every act of man. He has not commanded any man to be ungodly. He has not given any man license to sin.

Ὅτι πολλὴ σοφία τοῦ Κυρίου, ἰσχυρὸς ἐν δυναστείᾳ καὶ βλέπων τὰ πάντα. Καὶ οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τοὺς φοβουμένους αὐτὸν, καὶ αὐτὸς ἐπιγνώσεται πᾶν ἔργον ἀνθρώπου. Καὶ οὐκ ἐνετείλατο οὐδενὶ ἀσεβεῖν, καὶ οὐκ ἔδωκεν ἄνεσιν οὐδενὶ ἁμαρτάνειν.

Sirach · 15:18-20

World English Bible

Translation

He who has clean hands and a pure heart; who has not lifted up his soul to falsehood, and has not sworn deceitfully.

Original · Hebrew

נְקִ֥י כַפַּ֗יִם וּֽבַר־לֵ֫בָ֥ב אֲשֶׁ֤ר ׀ לֹא־נָשָׂ֣א לַשָּׁ֣וְא נַפְשִׁ֑י וְלֹ֖א נִשְׁבַּ֣ע לְמִרְמָֽה׃

the Psalms · 24:4

Translation

“‘You shall not take vengeance, nor bear any grudge against the children of your people; but you shall love your neighbor as yourself. I am Yahweh. The stranger who lives as a foreigner with you shall be to you as the native-born among you, and you shall love him as yourself; for you lived as foreigners in the land of Egypt. I am Yahweh your God.

Original · Hebrew

לֹֽא־תִקֹּ֤ם וְלֹֽא־תִטֹּר֙ אֶת־בְּנֵ֣י עַמֶּ֔ךָ וְאָֽהַבְתָּ֥ לְרֵעֲךָ֖ כָּמ֑וֹךָ אֲנִ֖י יְהוָֽה׃ כְּאֶזְרָ֣ח מִכֶּם֩ יִהְיֶ֨ה לָכֶ֜ם הַגֵּ֣ר ׀ הַגָּ֣ר אִתְּכֶ֗ם וְאָהַבְתָּ֥ לוֹ֙ כָּמ֔וֹךָ כִּֽי־גֵרִ֥ים הֱיִיתֶ֖ם בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם אֲנִ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃

the Torah (Leviticus) · 19:18, 34
